name: Game studios and app businesses
sector: 7.M Digital economy, social and public sector

problems.words: Client projects always run over and we eat the extra hours
quick_ideas: Compare estimated against actual hours on your last finished project, so you see where it slipped
Review each live project's hours against its estimate once a week.

workzap_build.text: a project tracker showing estimate against actual hours per milestone, with alerts as soon as a project starts to overrun.

problems.ask_first: How do you estimate a project at the start?
problems.free_stops: How hours are captured and alerts are set is covered in the solution document.

problems.words: Client change requests come in verbally, then scope disputes
quick_ideas: Write down every client ask and get it acknowledged before work starts
Keep all change requests for a project in one list, so scope is clear later.

workzap_build.text: a change-request log where every ask is recorded, estimated and approved by the client before work begins.

problems.free_stops: The approval flow goes in the solution document; contract terms are for your lawyer.

problems.words: Foreign clients pay late and we're short for salaries
quick_ideas: List all open invoices with their age, so the oldest get chased first
Invoice on the day a milestone is signed off, not at month-end.

workzap_build.text: a receivables ageing board with automated reminders to each client and a view of what's due before payroll.

problems.free_stops: The reminder schedule and runway view are detailed in the solution document.

problems.words: Revenue sits in AdMob, AppLovin, Play and App Store — no single view
quick_ideas: Pick the few numbers per title you really need and collect them once into one sheet
Check them on a fixed day, so drops are spotted early.

workzap_build.text: a unified revenue view pulling store and ad- network reports into one daily screen per title.

problems.free_stops: Which sources connect and how is set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Bugs get reported on WhatsApp and lost
quick_ideas: Agree that every bug goes into your tracker, not chat
Have one person move this week's chat reports into the tracker.

workzap_build.text: a bug intake form that pushes reports straight into the team's tracker.

problems.free_stops: The form and its connection to your tracker are designed in the solution document.

problems.words: Builds go out without proper QA
quick_ideas: Write a short release checklist and use it on the next build
Make one named role sign off before any submission.

workzap_build.text: a release checklist with QA sign-off that must be completed before a build is submitted.

problems.free_stops: The checklist content and sign-off flow are prepared in the solution document.

problems.words: We don't know who's overloaded and who's free
quick_ideas: Map who is on which project this week in one sheet
Review it before saying yes to new work.

workzap_build.text: a team capacity view showing allocation per person per week.

problems.free_stops: How allocation is captured and displayed goes in the solution document.

problems.words: Timesheets are guesswork, so billing clients is guesswork
quick_ideas: Ask the team to log hours per project at the end of each day, not each week
Check logged hours against what was billed on one recent project.

workzap_build.text: a lightweight daily timesheet via WhatsApp or web, tied straight to client billing.

problems.free_stops: The timesheet flow and billing link are detailed in the solution document.

problems.words: Support emails and store reviews pile up unanswered
quick_ideas: Give one person fixed daily time for reviews and support
Group repeated complaints, so the team sees which bug matters most.

workzap_build.text: a support inbox that triages store reviews and emails with saved replies and ageing.

problems.free_stops: The triage rules and reply library are set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Paying for licences and cloud nobody's using
quick_ideas: List every recurring tool and cloud cost once with its owner
Cancel or downgrade anything nobody claims.

workzap_build.text: a subscription and cloud spend register with renewal alerts and owner per item.

problems.free_stops: The register and alert set-up go in the solution document.

never_say: Benchmark retention, eCPM, revenue or salary figures, or promises a title will succeed. Advice on IP ownership, publishing contracts, NDAs or employment law — say "talk to a lawyer". Advice on data protection, children's privacy rules or store policy appeals. Tax, remittance or export-of-services advice — say "talk to your accountant". Help with fake installs, fake ratings, ad fraud or bypassing store rules; never ask for code, keys or console logins.

sample_reply.person: We do client work to fund our own games, but client projects always overrun. Any solution?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, there's a clear way to get on top of this, and you can start this week. 1 Compare estimated against actual hours on your last finished project, so you can see where it slipped. 2 Write down every client change request and get it acknowledged before work starts. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a tracker showing estimate against actual hours per milestone, alerts when a project starts overrunning, and a change log the client approves. Would you like me to prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
